effect.u_message: The tally lists loaves, waterskins and spare dressings. A different hand has cut across the last line: "Leave the wheel. Carry whoever can still breathe." A trail of harness leads back toward the ash-covered ground; scraping comes from behind the fold.

Pippin stood with his back to the wounded while the hammer widened this gap. A broken shield is caught beneath his heel. The men who passed him left lighter footprints beyond the ridge; his own never turned away.

The crossing split under a retreating crowd. Bloody handprints reach along the near rim and stop at the loose tissue. Farther west the firm ground curves around the opening; the sheet beside you covers a much shorter passage.

The line was built from shields already broken in the fighting. Splintered wood and scraps of cloak show how quickly it was thrown together. They left a narrow gap for the wounded. The tracks beyond it turn toward the great ribs.
